description:
Which NOTAMs were in force at a location at a given time, or at any moment of a time window?

Searches Airside Labs' capture of the FAA SWIM NOTAM feed. Returns one entry per distinct
NOTAM (re-broadcasts and the US domestic and ICAO text forms merged) with its number, decoded
start and end (`end_kind`: fixed, EST = estimated, PERM = permanent), schedule, Q-code and text,
and, if it was cancelled or replaced, by which NOTAM and when (`ended_early`). A NOTAM is in
force from its B) start until the earlier of its C) end and its cancellation or replacement;
one cancelled before its start never took effect. `in_force_rule` states the rule in full.

Give `at` (an instant) OR `start`/`end` (a window). With neither, the END OF CAPTURE is used,
not the current time, and a note says so. `location` is the ICAO location as in NOTAM item A):
an aerodrome (KJFK, EGLL) or a centre/FIR (KZNY, EGTT); a three-letter US code is answered with
a hint to the K- form. `text_contains` takes keywords that must all appear (case-insensitive,
literal: % and _ are ordinary characters), e.g. "RWY CLSD" or "ILS". `include_cancelled` also
lists NOTAMs whose published period covers the time but which had already been cancelled or
replaced, marked not in force. `limit` is 1..100 (default 40); `counts` says how many matched.


NOT FOR OPERATIONAL USE: this is Airside Labs' historical capture of the FAA SWIM NOTAM feed, for reference and analysis, not a NOTAM service; never use it for flight planning or a go/no-go decision, and say so when you quote it. It is redistributed by Airside Labs and is not endorsed by the FAA. Coverage is the feed's: heavily US-weighted, with some international locations; many non-US locations are absent. Reading the answer: `status` is one of resolved (NOTAMs found), none_in_force (the location is captured, the time is fully covered, and nothing captured was in force -- the strongest negative the data supports), none_captured (nothing found, but the time is not fully covered, so this is NOT evidence of none), not_captured (the capture holds nothing for this location or number -- never a statement that none existed), known_by_reference, ambiguous, unresolved (the input could not be looked up; the note says why) or unavailable. `capture` gives the capture window, when continuous daily capture began, and `warnings` for the time asked about; read it before concluding anything from an empty or short list. `provenance.source_id` and `provenance.edition` cite the capture the index was built from. Times are UTC. An unresolved or empty result is a real answer, not an error.
name: notam_search
title: Search captured NOTAMs
